issues.description: getCategoryLabel conflates label rendering with heuristic acronym guessing
issues.detail: The previous adapter had a small, explicit data table mapping category IDs to labels (one fact per row). The new lib/categories.ts replaces that table with a heuristic: split on hyphen, then guess acronym vs version vs default. This is COMPLECTED — it intertwines two concerns (the known category vocabulary as data) with code (the guess-rules for unknowns). The known vocabulary is a value; it should still be a value. A simple decomposition: keep the lookup map as the source of truth, and only fall through to the heuristic for unknowns, logging or surfacing the miss. As written, a future category like "s3" yields "S3" (fine), but "sso" yields "SSO" (probably fine), while something like "vpcflow" yields "Vpcflow" silently. The data is now hiding in regex.

issues.description: selectedPoint identity complects "which radar dot is highlighted" with "which category the selector shows"
issues.detail: In risk-radar-view-client.tsx, a single piece of state — selectedPoint (a RadarDataPoint) — is used to mean three different things: the dot the user clicked on the radar, the value the dropdown shows, and the row whose severity breakdown is displayed. These are not the same concern. The category selection is a value (categoryId: string | null); the selected radar dot is an identity in the chart view; the details panel is derived. Coupling them through one object reference means handleCategoryChange has to do a data.find() to reconstruct what is really just an id, and any future divergence (e.g., "highlight without selecting", or "keep selection across data refresh") will require unwinding this. Decompose: store selectedCategoryId: string | null as the single source of truth; derive selectedPoint via useMemo from data + id.

issues.description: CategorySelector encodes a sentinel string ("all") to mean null, then translates back — place-oriented signaling through a magic value
issues.detail: handleValueChange checks value === "" || value === "all" and converts to null; the Select then uses selectedCategory ?? "all" to render. Two encodings of the same fact (null vs the string "all") have to be kept in sync at every boundary. This is the kind of incidental complexity Hickey would name: the absence of a selection is a value (null/undefined), and the UI control needs a representation, but the translation belongs in one place, not scattered between the parent's prop, the child's value, and the child's handler. Either make "all" a real category id at the data layer or push the conversion into a tiny adapter so the rest of the code only sees string | null.

issues.description: HorizontalBarChart now computes maxValue on every render of every bar inside .map
issues.detail: Inside the items.map callback, maxValue is computed as Math.max(...data.map(d => d.value)) — once per bar, O(n) per item, O(n^2) overall. The previous code had the same shape inline only in the width string and was also wrong, but the new version makes it more visible without fixing the algorithmic cost. This is also a small place-oriented smell: the bar's width is a function of (item, data, total), but the data-derived value (max) is recomputed per element. Lift maxValue and total handling above the map (a const computed once, or useMemo) so each bar is a pure transformation of (item, max, total). Same correctness, less incidental work.

issues.description: Removing category badge from DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES while adding a labelFormatter path elsewhere — two filter-display systems now coexist
issues.detail: active-filter-badge.tsx drops the category__in entry, while findings-filters.tsx now passes labelFormatter, and data-table-filter-custom.tsx applies it inside the multi-select item. There are now two parallel mechanisms for "how a filter value is shown to the user": DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES (label + formatMultiple) and filter.labelFormatter (value-level). Category got moved from one system into the other without unifying them. A user filtering by category will see formatted labels in the dropdown, but the active-filter badge for category will fall back to the generic path. Either keep both representations consistent (formatter applies to badge too), or commit to a single value->label function as the canonical place. Right now the label of a category is in three places: the API string, the formatter, and the dropped badge entry.

issues.description: SEVERITY_ORDER now has two keys mapping to value 4 (Informational and Info)
issues.detail: The constants file adds Info: 4 alongside Informational: 4. This silently encodes "two names for the same thing" as data — fine if the API actually emits both spellings, but the file does not say so, and any consumer doing Object.keys(SEVERITY_ORDER) will now see seven entries with a duplicated rank. The fact being represented ("these two strings denote the same severity") is not the same as the fact being represented for the other five ("this name has this rank"). Either normalize the input at the boundary (map Info -> Informational on ingestion) or model the synonym explicitly. As written, the value is doing two jobs.

issues.description: SPECIAL_CASES is an empty map with a comment promising future entries
issues.detail: An empty Record with a TODO-style comment is speculation as code. It signals that the author expects the heuristic to fail and has pre-built an escape hatch — but until it's used, it's dead code that has to be maintained, tested, and reasoned about. If the heuristic is good enough, delete it. If it isn't, populate it now with the cases that motivated it. Empty data structures kept "just in case" are incidental complexity: they pretend to be a value but carry no facts.

issues.description: PR mixes a feature (Risk Radar + category filter) with a global rename ("Threat Score" -> "Prowler ThreatScore")
issues.detail: The diff to risk-plot-client.tsx and threat-score.tsx is a separate concern (product naming) from the radar feature. Bundling them complects review and revert: if the rename is wrong (e.g., marketing reverses), the radar work is entangled with it. Hammock question: was this one decision or two? It reads as two. Splitting would have made each change small and reviewable on its own terms.

review.summary: The PR ships a working feature, but several seams are easy rather than simple. The biggest one is replacing an explicit category-label data table with a heuristic in lib/categories.ts — the vocabulary stops being a value and becomes a guess, with an empty SPECIAL_CASES escape hatch that signals the author already knows the heuristic will miss. The radar view's selectedPoint state complects three concerns (which dot is highlighted, what the dropdown shows, what the details panel renders) when one selectedCategoryId would do, and the CategorySelector then encodes the absence of selection as the magic string \"all\" that has to be translated at every boundary. The filter-display layer now has two parallel mechanisms (DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES vs labelFormatter), and the bundled \"Threat Score\" rename is a separate decision riding along on a feature PR. None of this is broken; most of it is the kind of incidental complexity that compounds quietly. Keep the category vocabulary as data, store the selection as an id, and split product-rename commits from feature commits next time.
